summary: The candidate quickly located and fixed the sweep bug (tests went from failing to passing) but did so with almost no narration, no stated mechanism-level hypothesis, and no closing explanation of why the fix worked — a fast but opaque path to a correct fix.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate read the failing test output and noted the discrepancy between expected and actual units, but never posed a question or explicit hypothesis about what a partially-shipped hold should return before editing the code. They moved straight from noting the symptom to vague exploration.

Their stated plan was to dig around in the release path and watch hold state fields — this names a location, not a mechanism. They never articulated that the sweep was releasing the original count instead of the remaining count before making the edit.

There are only two speech lines in the whole session, and neither one narrates what was found while reading the code or explains the specific fix being made; the actual edit and save happen with no narration at all.

The edit to src/sweep.ts was made quickly and did in fact resolve the failing test, so the fix was scoped correctly even though the reasoning behind it was never verbalized. There is no evidence of thrashing or unrelated edits.
After editing, they reran the full test suite and confirmed it passed before ending the session, which is the minimum verification step expected.

The session ended immediately after the tests passed with no explanation of why releasing the original count caused phantom stock or why the remaining-count fix addresses it; the candidate simply ended the session on green.
